Now, what is surprising or wrong about the data?
LOOK AT THIS:
In UniProt, human UGT2A1 has accession P0DTE4. Its canonical sequence length in Swiss-Prot is listed as 422 amino acids!
HOWEVER:
1. In NCBI RefSeq and Ensembl, the canonical protein (MANE Select, NP_006789.2, ENST00000286604 / ENSP00000286604) is 527 amino acids!
2. Most human UDP-glucuronosyltransferases (UGT2 family, such as UGT2A2, UGT2A3, UGT2B4, UGT2B7, UGT2B15, etc.) are ~527-530 amino acids.
3. In UniProt, P0DTE4 was reviewed with length 422 aa (which corresponds to an alternatively spliced isoform lacking exon 3/part of the catalytic/substrate domain, 105 amino acids missing), while the full-length 527 aa form is the principal/canonical isoform in RefSeq/Ensembl/MANE Select!
4. What about ING4?
   In UniProt, ING4 (Q9UNL4) has canonical length 249 amino acids (RefSeq NP_057246.1 is 249 aa; Ensembl canonical ENST00000341550 is 248 aa).
5. If UGT2A1 is 527 aa and ING4 is 249 aa:
   527 / 249 = 2.116 >= 2, so YES (527 is at least twice 249).
6. If UGT2A1 is taken from UniProt P0DTE4 (422 aa) and ING4 is 249 aa:
   422 / 249 = 1.695 < 2, so NO.
